A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCOUT research work. All 22 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including Appendices A–G, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, figures, and implementation listings.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent-training experiments on six game tasks, baseline comparisons, computational costs, sequential learning, and appendix scout-training curves and perplexity measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds 7B-model results, weak-scout robustness, visual-task evaluations, harder-cube generalization, and NLP benchmark results.

M1.justification: The exploration–distillation–multi-turn-PPO pipeline, losses, and original architectures remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds a limited multimodal adaptation using image observations, Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, and CNN vision scouts instead of the original symbolic/text observations; its implementation is only briefly described.

E1.justification: v3 retains the six original game tasks and adds visual-observation FrozenLake and Sokoban, harder Rubik’s Cube instances at Rotations 4–5, and nine NLP benchmarks: MMLU, BoolQ, GSM8K, ARC-c, ARC-e, NQ-open, PIQA, TriviaQA, and WinoG. These substantially broaden input conditions, task difficulty, and application domains.

E2.justification: The evaluated reference models expand to unadapted Qwen2.5-7B-It and Qwen2.5-VL-3B-It with direct-RL variants, plus the Visual Scout in Table 5. The original Scout-DQN/PPO, RAGEN/multi-turn PPO, State Estimation RL, SPA, and five large-model comparators remain. No new competing RL algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: Additional experimental designs include 7B and vision-language backbones, initialization from a scout checkpoint at 10% of training, and zero-shot evaluation from lower cube rotation depths to higher depths (Tables 4–6). These substantially extend the evaluation design. Previously documented training settings in Appendix D remain unchanged; the new vision and NLP evaluation protocols are incompletely specified.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of dependence on scout quality using an under-converged teacher (Table 4), robustness to visual observations described as partially observable (Table 5), and extrapolation across cube difficulty (Table 6). These address substantive robustness and generalization questions beyond v1’s retained sequential-learning analysis, training curves, and reasoning example.

E5.justification: The existing scout uncertainty entries in Table 1 are retained. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explanation of uncertainty estimation. The additional studies report point estimates without extending statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original results are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 1 reports a 7B SCOUT average of 0.88 versus 0.48 for its multi-turn-PPO baseline. Tables 4–6 report weak-scout final scores of 0.60/0.98, visual-task scores of 0.95/0.95, and Rotation-3-trained performance of 0.58/0.45 on Rotations 4/5. Appendix Table 10 reports NLP averages of 0.56 for the base model and 0.60 with SCOUT. These are added evaluations, not improvements to the earlier matched results.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, objectives and equations (1)–(7), and appendix notation are retained. Calling the visual environments POMDPs does not introduce a mathematical observation model, revised derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the exploration-bottleneck argument, three-stage contribution, 0.86 headline score, and approximately 60% GPU-cost saving. The conclusion additionally claims generalization to POMDP environments and different task difficulties, modestly extending the stated contribution.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets weak-scout results as transferring useful knowledge despite imperfect demonstrations, visual results as overcoming dependence on lossless symbolic observations, and cube results as extrapolation to unseen complexity. Appendix B’s limitations remain unchanged, including the now-inconsistent statement that models larger than 3B were not evaluated.

D1.justification: v3 supplies limited operational details for the additions, notably the 10%-training scout checkpoint and the named vision-language backbone with CNN scouts. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, architecture listings, textualization instructions, and code-access information are retained. Detailed visual and NLP evaluation recipes are not added.

R1.justification: Appendix C and the bibliography add Luo et al.’s Chunk-level GRPO and Mask-GRPO works to the discussion of RL algorithm improvements. The positioning of SCOUT relative to agent RL, classical exploration, and large–small model collaboration otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts two experimental subsections, a robustness paragraph, and a short conclusion extension; the existing implicit-to-explicit modeling section becomes Section 4.6. Affiliations, proceedings information, and acknowledgements also change. Most existing prose and the overall main-text/appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Result presentation expands substantially through new robustness, vision, difficulty-transfer, and NLP tables (Tables 4–6 and 10), plus a 7B block in Table 1. Figures 1–5 retain their content. The earlier appendix Tables 4–7 become Tables 7, 8, 9, and 11; their relocation and resulting pagination changes do not constitute new evidence.

improvement.justification: The weak-scout and harder-cube experiments provide useful evidence about teacher dependence and generalization that v1 lacked, while the original findings remain intact. The overall gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new vision/NLP evaluations and unchanged uncertainty reporting. Table 5 claims cross-task transfer without identifying transfer-specific results, and Appendix B still denies evaluation beyond 3B despite the new 7B rows. These gaps limit how strongly the expanded applicability claims can be supported.
